channel.title: Wire — AI
channel.description: AI from thirty sources, one digest a day.

item.title: Postgres 19 is Late, and It's AI's Fault
item.description: LLMs are finding bugs faster than committers can fix them (2 sources: lobsters, postgresweekly)

item.title: Anthropic's internal AI use, at retail prices, now exceeds its employee pay
item.description: Anthropic's IPO filing reveals a striking milestone: Its internal AI usage is now valued above employee compensation. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Anthropic reports $17B in Q3 revenue, commitments of $895B in revised S-1
item.description: Anthropic unveiled its S-1 prospectus last week, but the initial filing only included the company's financials through the first half of the year. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: AI delivers 'zero financial payoff' to most companies, Apollo economist says
item.description: "Despite massive investments and widespread hype around artificial intelligence, the technology has delivered zero financial payoff to corporate America outside of tech." (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Uber Builds MCP Gateway to Govern Access to 800+ Servers and 5,000+ AI Agent Tools
item.description: Uber has built an MCP Gateway to standardize how AI agents discover and invoke internal services across more than 800 MCP servers and 5,000 tools. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: Article: Systemic Approach to Memory, Knowledge, and Context in Agentic AI Architectures
item.description: The article argues that reliable agentic AI architecture depends on a context engine that selects, injects, compresses, and expires information before it reaches the model. (1 source: infoq)

item.title: An easy way to try local AI with braindead-local-intelligence
item.description: In this blog post, I present braindead-local-intelligence, a project to easily run local LLM and image generation models on Linux with podman (1 source: lobsters)

item.title: Import AI 479: Spacewar; low-latency tasks versus LLMs; Genie 4
item.description: Welcome to Import AI, a newsletter about AI research. Import AI runs on arXiv, cappuccinos, and feedback from readers. If you’d like to support this, please subscribe. (1 source: importai)

item.title: It wasn't AI that flipped Proton's charge
item.description: Proton's CEO called a request for security testing "loser thinking". Using AI to write code is fine, but for a privacy company, the guardrails around that code are the product. (1 source: hackernews)

item.title: Scheme+ language : 100% Scheme compatible, infix support and now with type annotation and inference for performance.
